subject: [GSoC-R] Mentors: We need your input NOW!

messages.author: b98e21751c27e8b9
messages.subject: [GSoC-R] Mentors: We need your input NOW!
parts:
Mentors:

We *really* need you to comment on your student proposals. We have a
very large number of high quality proposals, and need to make slot
requests from Google.

We really need you to help Toby and me by commenting on the strengths
and weaknesses of each proposal for one of your project ideas.

Any proposal that does not have (detailed, positive) comments from at
least two of the proposed project mentors isn't going to get a slot.

Google also requires you to select 'Want to Mentor' for the proposal.
We need at least two mentors to (provisionally) slot the project.

Google's deadline is coming up, and I will err on the side of
requesting fewer slots if we don't have input. Please get your initial
input into the summerofcode system this weekend and make sure you've
selected 'Want to Mentor' if you have a "truly excellent" proposal
(those are Google's words, not mine).

If you have additional questions for the students, you are encouraged
to continue communicating with the student to work them out. Please
don't telegraph strong/weak proposal feelings, and you must not promise
or hint at acceptance rejection (it is against Google program rules, as
I've previously shared).

We are refining the min/max slot request numbers daily as we review
proposals and get more feedback from mentors. We are starting to
provisionally star strong proposals with clear mentor support. Your
input is critical over the next several days for us to make a well-
informed request to Google. Please help us out.

Students:

As just described above, you may receive communication from mentors on
your proposals. If you do, please respond as quickly as possible. The
clock is ticking to slot requests to Google, and we are instructed to
take student communication into account in granting slots once we've
received a slot allocation from Google.

As always, please reach out to Toby or me if you have any questions or
concerns.

Regards,

Brian
